items.statement: Renewable energy revenue nearly doubled YoY to INR 259 crores in Q2 FY26, driven by new capacities and rate differentials
items.quote: Aditya Birla renewables revenue nearly doubled on a year-on-year basis to INR259 crores, led by newer capacities and onetime revenue of INR50 crores on account of rate differential.

items.statement: Global caustic prices softened 5% (CFR SEA), but domestic prices remained stable due to demand and rupee depreciation
items.quote: While the global caustic prices have softened with CFR SEA down by 5%, domestic caustic prices stood higher due to stable demand and rupee depreciation.

items.statement: Chlorine derivative capacity increased by 11 KTPA in Q2 FY26; ECH and CPVC projects on track for Q3 FY26 mechanical completion
items.quote: The mechanical completion is expected by Q3 FY '26. Post completion of ongoing projects, chlorine integration is expected to reach 70% compared to current 64%.

items.statement: Cellulosic fiber blended realization supported by specialty fiber volume mix improvement to 24% and currency depreciation
items.quote: Specialty fiber volume mix improved to 24%, led by higher exports of specialty fibers, improved product mix and currency depreciation supported blended realization of CSF.

items.statement: Cellulosic fashion yarn sales volume grew 3% YoY in Q2 FY26 led by festive demand
items.quote: Cellulosic fashion yarn sales volume grew by 3% year-on-year, led by festive demand.

items.statement: Cement sales volume grew 6.9% YoY to 33.85 million metric tons in Q2 FY26, supported by infrastructure capex
items.quote: The consolidated sales volume were up by 6.9% year-on-year to 33.85 million metric tons.

items.statement: Financial services lending portfolio (NBFC + housing finance) grew 29% YoY to INR 1.78 lakh crores in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Total lending portfolio, that is NBFC, and housing finance stood highest ever at nearly INR1,78,000 crores, up 29% year-on-year.

items.statement: Assets under management (AMC, life, health insurance) grew 10% YoY to INR 5.5 lakh crores in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Total assets under management of AMC, Life and Health insurance grew by 10% year-on-year at nearly INR550,000 crores.

items.statement: Birla Opus premium/luxury products revenue contribution was 65% in Q2 FY26, including emulsion enamel, wood finish, and waterproofing
items.quote: The premium and luxury products revenue contribution was upwards at 65% of revenue, covering all categories across emulsion enamel, wood finish and waterproofing, including retail and institutional segment.

items.statement: Cellulosic fibers sales volume lower by 5% YoY in Q2 FY26 due to logistics issues at Vilayat (now normalized)
items.quote: Total sales volume of CSF was lower by 5% year-on-year due to logistics-related issues at Vilayat, which is now normalized.

items.statement: Cellulosic fashion yarn realizations impacted by cheaper imports from China
items.quote: The realizations continue to remain impacted by cheaper imports from China.

items.statement: Caustic soda sales volume flat in Q2 FY26 due to constrained production from lower power availability
items.quote: Caustic sales volume for the quarter were flat due to constrained production on account of lower power availability.

items.statement: Chlorine derivative profitability impacted by negative realizations
items.quote: The improvement in caustic prices led to higher ECU, which was partially impacted by increasing negative chlorine realizations.

items.statement: Cellulosic fibers China demand impacted by property freeze, weak household confidence, and delayed capex decisions
items.quote: China is not in an acute crisis, but in a structurally lower growth orbit. Property demand is frozen, household confidence is weak and private entrepreneurs are holding back capex decisions.

items.statement: Cellulosic fibers Q3 FY26 performance depends on U.S. tariffs and global pulp prices
items.quote: We expect a slightly better performance in Q3. But obviously, there are a lot of ifs and buts in terms of U.S. tariffs, in terms of global pulp prices.

items.statement: Chemicals profitability depends on caustic prices and chlorine demand in India
items.quote: The honest answer to that is it essentially depends on chloride, given our large exposure still to the chloralkali business. It's a combination of caustic prices and chlorine demand in India.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue impact from U.S. tariffs and cotton duty removal
items.quote: quarter 3 is also equally impacted in these 2 businesses. But RSWM has 6 business segments. So, these 3 are the ones impacted. The other 3 are comparatively less impacted. So, that impact we are expecting to be limited in the third quarter.

items.statement: ₹92 crore capex for knit division modernization and printing facility
items.quote: the company has planned to invest almost ₹92 crores in the modernization and upgradation of the knit division and this will also give us an additional product mix as we are adding a printing facility during this expansion.

items.statement: ₹60 crore capex for 60 MW round-the-clock renewable power
items.quote: have invested significantly in 70 megawatts of renewable energy, 10 megawatts behind the meter, which we shared in the previous call also and 60 megawatts of round-the-clock power, which the Board had cleared a few days

items.statement: ₹55 crore modernization capex budget for FY26
items.quote: the figure for modernization CAPEX for the year '25-'26, we have approved a budget of ₹55 crores

items.statement: Knit and mélange order book impacted by U.S. tariffs and buyer renegotiations
items.quote: many knit consumers in India are selling garments to the U.S., and U.S. customers have asked for strong discounts. So, that has impacted. RSWM's utilization of the knit business is impacted during this period.

items.statement: Gross margin expansion due to lower raw material costs and product mix
items.quote: gross margin expanding to 38.4%, a 195-basis point improvement YoY and 116 basis point QoQ improvement, primarily led by lower raw material costs and a more profitable product mix.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement due to cost management
items.quote: EBITDA margin improving sharply to 6.8% compared to 3.6% last year, a 318-bps expansion, primarily driven by the operational efficiency, disciplined cost management

items.statement: Cotton yarn price reduction due to import duty removal and U.S. tariffs
items.quote: the price reduction of cotton yarn has been to the tune of ₹8 to ₹10 for domestic and from 10 to 15 cents in exports.

items.statement: Renewable energy cost savings per unit
items.quote: this will definitely reduce our energy cost per unit to the extent of almost ₹1.

items.statement: Annual renewable energy savings estimate
items.quote: the savings will be to the tune of ₹30 crores to ₹40 crores at this.

items.statement: Domestic volume growth to be consistent with slight market share creep in next few quarters
items.quote: I think -- so I see that there should be a consistent trend on the domestic volume growth. There could be a bit up and down from one quarter to the other. But from a medium to long-term point of view, we see that we should be able to maintain and slightly creep up our market share as we go along in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Export volumes to remain choppy for next few months, medium-term growth expected
items.quote: As far as exports are concerned, I see it to be a bit choppy at least for the next few months. But then clearly, medium-term growth will be there.

items.statement: U.S. export volumes impacted by tariffs, but long-term growth trajectory remains positive
items.quote: we were positively growing in the U.S., and this has kind of been a bit of a holdback for the time being. I look at it from that point of view. But then we're also looking then to increase our focus in some of the other markets and also talking to see how we can increase volumes in some of the other geographies.

items.statement: Domestic demand robust, FY26 volumes to stay positive by year-end
items.quote: I think clearly the plan was to grow much more stronger in the year. And -- but I'm quite positive that we should stay positive by the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Growth expected in FY27 despite near-term challenges
items.quote: we'll have to consider this as a normal and take this as the operating environment. And we are positive that there will be growth in FY '27, too.

items.statement: TDQ capacity expansion at Dahej on track; trial production expected in H1 CY26 (Jan-Jun 2026)
items.quote: Our ongoing TDQ capacity investment at Dahej remains on track and we anticipate commissioning and trial production in H1 calendar year 2026.

items.statement: Domestic volumes ~2/3 of total; exports ~1/3
items.quote: I think maybe, I would say, about two-third, one-third, you can say, take a ratio. Two-third domestic, one-third exports.

items.statement: Domestic rubber chemicals demand estimated at 80,000-85,000 tons/year; NOCIL targets 40% share
items.quote: we are looking at 80,000 to 85,000 tons of demand per annum, in which NOCIL share is about -- we normally target about 40% as a market share.

items.statement: Operational efficiencies to improve margins; steam, electricity, and hydrogen consumption reductions to kick in by Q4 FY26
items.quote: quite a few initiatives that are already underway, are in place so that we really can improve our steam efficiencies, reduce steam consumption on a per unit basis, looking at our electricity consumptions, looking at our hydrogen consumption, for example. So these are all things which are more or less in advanced stages. We should start seeing them kick in before quarter 4 of this

items.statement: Pricing pressure bottoming out; cautious optimism on further deflation
items.quote: I'm kind of, let's say, cautious optimism that it's kind of bottoming out, let's say that.

items.statement: Indian tire industry robust due to government infra push and GST rate reduction; replacement market to benefit
items.quote: The Indian tire industry continues to remain robust on the back of government's continued infra push and demand side interventions. The reduction in GST rates is expected to stimulate demand for vehicles and tires.

items.statement: Soda Ash pricing to remain range-bound for rest of FY26
items.quote: Overall, we expect the pricing to be subdued in the current range and remain there for the rest of the year.

items.statement: US export pricing to remain tough in Southeast Asia, domestic pricing range-bound
items.quote: On the export side, while many markets are okay, it is turning out to be tough in terms of the Southeast Asian market. So, we will come back with specific number on the export side only. The domestic should remain pretty much in the range we have been doing last 2 years.

items.statement: UK EBITDA to turn positive by Q4 FY26
items.quote: We do expect to turn positive in the 3rd quarter of this year and definitely moving to positive by 4th quarter of this year in UK.

items.statement: Kenya volumes to recover in H2 FY26 after shipment delays
items.quote: in UK. Kenya saw lower sales volume due to shipment delays. However, in the second half of the year, we should see the volumes come back because most of the shipment issues have been resolved

items.statement: India Soda Ash demand robust, pricing stabilized post anti-dumping duty (ADD) notice
items.quote: The market is the same and stable because there are two issues that have happened. One is the anti-dumping notice itself has given a salutary effect in terms of imports coming down a bit and the pressure on pricing going away.

items.statement: India Soda Ash volumes to grow by 30,000+ tonnes YoY in Q2 FY26
items.quote: If you look at the India number for the Soda Ash broadly, it is up quarter-on-quarter, basically from previous year, same quarter to this quarter by about 30,000-odd tonnes.

items.statement: India salt volumes to grow by 50,000+ tonnes YoY in Q2 FY26
items.quote: If you look at the salt number, it is almost up by about 50,000-odd tonnes. That is because of the new capacities which have come.

items.statement: India FOS capacity utilization to reach 80% by Q3 FY26, adding 5,000 tonnes
items.quote: the focus is entirely ensuring that the FOS unit quickly reaches 80% utili zation so that , we can add another 5 ,000 tonnes

items.statement: India Soda Ash capacity to increase by 500,000 tonnes in phases (150,000 tonnes quick, 350,000 tonnes later)
items.quote: We do believe that there is a component of growth which we should be doing in India in terms of the Soda Ash, at least another half a million tonne, 150,000 tonnes of that should come very quickly. The 350,000 tonnes will take a little time, but we will bring it in two steps.

items.statement: Global Soda Ash market to remain range-bound, normalization expected in 18 months due to capacity reconfiguration
items.quote: The market is going to remain range-bound in the current level. And it will start to ease as the geopolitics and the pressures come off due to reconfiguring of capacities, both in Europe and in China.

items.statement: CAPEX for FY26 and FY27 to remain ~Rs. 1,000 crores, with detailed plans shared in Q3 FY26
items.quote: It is going to be around that number, Abhijeet. In 3rd quarter, we will give you much better color.

items.statement: Top-line growth expected to accelerate to double-digit levels in coming quarters
items.quote: we should be looking at getting to double digits in due course, because there seems to be a very positive sentiment around consumer goods and especially foods. So, I do think this is our moment and it will definitely bring us the kind of growth that we have been missing for some time.

items.statement: Top-line growth expected to exceed 9% due to grammage increases and GST normalization
items.quote: growth, it doesn't work absolutely mathematically, 9 plus 6 is 15, we know that. But we are hoping that we get to 9 plus 6, but we could even get more than that.

items.statement: Volume and revenue growth to improve sequentially post-GST normalization
items.quote: we are seeing a very positive impact of this. And we are hoping that as we go forward, this will only become better.

items.statement: Margins to be sustained through cost-saving initiatives and commodity price stability
items.quote: sustain margins enabled by cost-saving initiatives and commodity situation, as I said, looks pretty good and we hope that that continues.

items.statement: Advertising spends normalized to pre-inflation levels
items.quote: last quarter, I think we have normalized our advertising spends and it will continue at that rate.

items.statement: Additional capacity being added in North plant for wafers
items.quote: wafers, again, is the fifth consecutive quarter of healthy double-digit growth, augmented by additional capacity that we are putting up in our plant in North.

items.statement: Market share gains expected in East region post-distribution stabilization
items.quote: we have stabilized to a large extent, I wouldn't say 100%, but we are almost 90% there. And things are looking good in the East and we hope to continue that momentum

items.statement: Market share gains in South region to drive double-digit growth
items.quote: The growths there have to be getting to double digits and that's what we are going to drive there.

items.statement: Margins to face slight pressure due to competitive pricing in regional markets
items.quote: there might be some changes in the margin structure, because I think if we have to get aggressive top-line growth, then we might have to look at a slight haircut as far as margins are concerned.

items.statement: Pricing growth in Q2 FY26 was 7-8% before GST changes
items.quote: the pricing growth was approximately 7% to 8%. And now with the GST changes, etc., the pricing is very different.

items.statement: GST normalization to reduce pricing impact in next quarter
items.quote: the pricing impact would be less than what it was.

items.statement: Underlying demand environment positive for consumer goods, especially food
items.quote: there seems to be a very positive sentiment around consumer goods and especially foods. So, I do think this is our moment.

items.statement: Cheese demand to recover post-inflationary slowdown
items.quote: I think this will certainly come back because this has been probably the only year where on a cheese growth, we have seen a slight deceleration.

items.statement: Volume growth of 6% in personal mobility, 8% in CVO, double-digit in industrial
items.quote: our personal mobility has grown at over 6%. Our CVO has grown at about 8% and industrial is in good double digits

items.statement: Rural B2C volume contribution ~25-30%, growing double-digit
items.quote: close to 25% of our B2C volumes are now beginn ing to come from rural and growing in double digits

items.statement: Lubricant volume of 60 million liters in Q3 FY26
items.quote: 60 million liters in this quarter

items.statement: CVO volume contribution ~38-40% of total
items.quote: CVO does about 38%, 40%

items.statement: Personal mobility volume contribution ~48-50% of total
items.quote: personal mobility is balance, which is 48%, 50%

items.statement: Base oil and forex volatility pressures
items.quote: The market conditions this quarter remained volatile with base oil fluctuations and out-of-range forex movements adding pressure

items.statement: Macroeconomic headwinds and tech shifts
items.quote: we are mindful of the external e nvironment, including the global macroeconomic headwinds and shifts in technology

items.statement: Launch of Castrol All-in-One Helmet Cleaner
items.quote: highlight of the quarter was launch of new products tailored to emerging consumer needs. Let me talk about the Castrol All-in-One Helmet Cl eaner, an innovative foam spray solution addressing helmet hygiene for 2-wheeler riders

items.statement: Revised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 12-14% (up from 10-12%)
items.quote: we wanted to extend our guidance from 10% to 12% to 12% to 14% for this fiscal year.

items.statement: Long-term revenue growth average of 10-12% with new retail business
items.quote: we indicate a long-term growth average of about 10% to 12% now with this new retail business as well.

items.statement: Fabric and apparel traditional business volume/value growth ~15% YoY in Q2 FY26
items.quote: overall growth for fabric and apparel, the traditional business has been about 15% in that range.

items.statement: ZECODE and DEVO combined revenue ~INR30 cr in H1 FY26
items.quote: the overall top line for the first half is approximately under INR30 crores.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment improving, festive season boosted retail activity in Q2 FY26
items.quote: the early arrival of the festive season boosted retail activity, leading to higher footfalls and better sales performance.

items.statement: GST cut on apparel expected to lift consumer sentiment and discretionary spending
items.quote: the recent cut in GST on selected apparel categories is expected to further lift consumer sentiment and encourage more spending.

items.statement: GST reduction and festive season boosted consumer sentiment in Q2 FY26
items.quote: GST reduction in apparel and other discretionary consumer items has definitely had a positive sentiment in the market.

items.statement: Gaining market share in branded apparel due to consumer aspiration and formalization
items.quote: we are gaining some market share. But as a company and as a brand, I think the branded players, there is more aspiration towards the brand.

items.statement: ZECODE and DEVO stores opened 9 in Q2 FY26 (7 ZECODE, 2 DEVO)
items.quote: we opened 7 new ZECODE stores and 2 new DEVO stores, bringing the total store count to 23 ZECODE and 12 DEVO stores.

items.statement: Retail stores (ZECODE/DEVO) have low gross margins, require scale for profitability
items.quote: both these businesses will work better at scale, particularly the fast fashion business, which needs a lot of scale to operate given that it has low gross margin.

items.statement: Retail stores initially company-owned, leased for 9-12 years
items.quote: The stores that we will open in the initial phase will all be company-owned. And these will be all on lease. So anywhere between 9 to 12 years kind of a lease.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for legacy business: ~14%, retail business to reduce by 150 bps
items.quote: we will stick to our original guidance of approximately 14% of EBITDA margin without this retail business, which we have indicated earlier, which will have a hit on EBITDA by about 150 basis points.

items.statement: DEVO pricing: Kurta Pyjama starts at INR1,700-2,000, goes up to INR10,000-12,000
items.quote: for example, Kurta Pyjama, which is an important category in the business, we have a starting price of approximately INR1,700 to INR2,000, and it goes all the way up to INR10,000, INR12,000.

items.statement: Motor OD claims ratio to reduce by ~5% in H2 FY26
items.quote: in H2, if you were to look at, we would certainly want this number to at least come down by about 5 percentage points for H2.

items.statement: Auto sector growth expected to sustain in H2 FY26
items.quote: So it is things are looking up. And we only wait to see if the momentum in the auto sales sustains in the month of November, December.

items.statement: Motor premium growth of 5.4% in October FY26 (vs. industry degrowth of 1.5%)
items.quote: Chola MS had a growth of 5.4% in the month of October, which means that our YTD, year-to-date degrowth that we had reported at the half year is now getting reduced as at YTD October.

items.statement: Crop insurance loss impact to reduce to ~INR150 cr in H2 FY26
items.quote: The crop, we have digested a good portion of the deficit that we had written last year. So there will be some more about at best another INR150 crores, which will get impact the growth in H2.

items.statement: Combined ratio (CoR) to improve from 109% (H1 FY26) due to reinsurance commissions
items.quote: Now actually, as we go along and when this 1/n premium starts coming into the P&L segment, our reinsurance commissions will also start going up, and we should see a bounce back into the overall profitability.

items.statement: Motor OD loss ratios to improve due to GST cut on parts (5% vs. 12%)
items.quote: The GST change that is coming in, in terms of the GST on parts prices, coming down from 12% to 5% will also give us some advantage as we go along as the severity of the claims will now go down.

items.statement: Reinsurance business (INR570 cr in H1 FY26) has better economic CoR than core business
items.quote: the economic combined ratio of this business is better than th e combined ratio on the core business. So it only operates to bring down the overall combined

items.statement: Motor TP reserving (10% higher than peers) adds ~3% to CoR
items.quote: our reserving level that what we are doing is at least 10% higher than many of our peers. And in our book, that translates into an effect of at least 3% on the CoR.

items.statement: Expense ratio (30.5% H1 FY26) below glide path target (29.1% without 1/n)
items.quote: The expense of management for Chola MS for the half year stood at 30.5%, which measured without 1/n works out to 29.1% and is lower than the glide path plan approved by t he Board

items.statement: Motor TP premiums unchanged for 4 years; no price hike yet
items.quote: the continued absence of increase in motor third-party premium for the last 4 years

items.statement: Motor TP price hike expected from April FY27 (industry hopeful)
items.quote: I would tend to think that industry will be very happy even if it comes in from April 1.

items.statement: Motor business mix: 52% cars, 37% commercial vehicles, 12% 2-wheelers
items.quote: Within motor, the company had a composition of 52% in cars 37% in commercial vehicles and 12% in 2-wheelers.

items.statement: 2-wheeler business reduced (TP premium degrowth) due to Board’s strategic call
items.quote: we have actually brought down from 5.4% to 4.7% in motor TP. So that is what is impacting the leverage.

items.statement: Health/PA segment mix at ~40% (down from 46-47% earlier)
items.quote: our benefit mix, if you were to look at on the overall health business, it would still be at around close to around 40% and it has come off from the level of 46%, 47% that used to be in earlier years.

items.statement: Motor OD claims ratio elevated due to competitive intensity; 8% higher than peers
items.quote: The motor OD claims ratio has been higher and also reflects the competitive intensity in the industry.

items.statement: Crop insurance loss (INR383 cr H1 FY26) due to retender impact
items.quote: Chola MS suffered a loss of crop insurance business consequent to the retender, which impacted the quarter's GDPI by about INR323 crores and INR383 crores for the half year.

items.statement: ROE target: 16-18% in near term
items.quote: Yes, that is the direction with which the management team is certainly working for, and we certainly expect to get closer to those levels.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance pending resolution of JJM fund issue
items.quote: I think projects, I don't want to take a call because this issue has been there for quite some time. As soon as this is resolved, which I expect very shortly, we will be coming out with our projections.

items.statement: Domestic product order book at record high INR 422 crores
items.quote: Order booking and backlog continued to improve, reaching the highest ever level of INR 422 crores.

items.statement: JJM project exposure reduced to INR 1,100 crores, mostly in final stages
items.quote: Our entire exposure is now down to about 1,100 crores, and which is all in the last 30% stages.

items.statement: O&M order backlog at INR 600 crores
items.quote: We have an order backlog of roughly about 600 crores in this sector.

items.statement: Domestic product demand improving due to new products, market share gains, and diversified segments
items.quote: No, I think the company felt we have done well, we have introduced new products. So, we have a very good export market supporting this. Our international supplies have increased. items.statement: International project demand expected to boost in H2 FY26 due to South African seasonality and new contracts
items.quote: Internationally, the third-4th Quarter is going to be much better because most of our business is in South Africa, the project business, and their execution picks up in this half.

items.statement: Naval and power sector inquiries improving
items.quote: We are seeing strong inquiries from the Power Division as well as we are seeing some kind of inquiry from the Naval Division.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to stabilize at 16-20%
items.quote: Our margin profile is between 16 to 20 and that is something we have maintained. The last quarter was a blip because of certain acquisitions which happened and certain one-time expenses which were captured. So, this is a normalized level and we expect to maintain this going forward.

items.statement: International project margins recovering to 18-20% EBITDA
items.quote: Margin profile, this quarter itself, our standalone was 20% EBITDA and consolidated was 18.87%. The first half was 17.78% and consolidated 16%. So, I think our margins have recovered in the 2nd Quarter, as we had mentioned, and this recovery will continue through the second half.

items.statement: Domestic project execution improving, O&M revenue expected to pick up in H2 FY26
items.quote: We have reached a high degree of completion and commissioning of these projects, which should place us very well to, once the outlook improves, to benefit to be a big beneficiary there.

items.statement: JJM payments delayed due to center-state fund resolution issue, expected to improve in H2 FY26
items.quote: The only problem is the timeline is being shifted on a regular basis. We had expected in the budget last year, this year's budget in February. But it's November now and the resolution is still anticipated. However, I think things are moving and we should get some positive news shortly.

items.statement: Domestic project execution dependent on policy resolution, cautious outlook
items.quote: Domestically, it is completely dependent on policy, both center state policy, how it moves, and we will be cautious. We are cautiously moving.

items.statement: Authorized capital increased for future inorganic opportunities, no immediate plans
items.quote: We are increasing our authorized capital, giving us the flexibility to raise capital. We have no immediate plan.

items.statement: O&M revenue expected to reach INR 70-100 crores by FY27
items.quote: We are looking at about 70 to 100 crores of O&M revenue.

items.statement: FY26 full-year guidance of INR 828 crore advanced sales achieved in Q2, with 50% of FY26 guidance met in first two quarters.
items.quote: this has resulted in our highest ever quarterly bookings and showing it at INR 828 crores of advanced sales, thereby showcasing over 50% of our full year guidance coming in just these two quarters.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 sales value of INR 720 crore (tripled YoY) and H1 FY26 sales of INR 828 crore (48% YoY growth).
items.quote: The company has achieved its highest ever quarterl y sales with sales value tripling Y-o-Y basis, which is to INR 720 crores, which is sales adding up to INR 828 crores, which is 48% Y-o-Y growth

items.statement: FY26 revenue visibility of INR 3,599 crore (INR 1,582 crore from committed sales, INR 2,017+ crore from inventory).
items.quote: The total visibility from this stands at about INR 3,599 crores, comprising INR 1,582 crores from the committed sales and about INR 2,000-plus crores from the available inventory to sale and revenue to recognize upon the life cycle.

items.statement: Upcoming launch pipeline expected to contribute INR 4,357 crore (GDV of 7 projects).
items.quote: Additionally, our upcoming launch pipeline is also expected to contribute INR 4,357 crores, which is the GDV of the balance seven projects.

items.statement: Overall revenue visibility of INR 8,000+ crore with strong growth momentum.
items.quote: And that's why the overall revenue visibility is at a robust number of sub INR 8,000 crores with a strong growth momentum ahead.

items.statement: FY26 delivery target of 1,000 possessions, with 533 homes already delivered in H1 FY26.

items.quote: Manhattan 1 as a project, we should be able to complete, our target is by next year, December. But in RERA timelines, obviously, they are higher, but our target is between December FY '26 to March FY '27 is what we are looking at completing it.

items.statement: Domino’s Sri Lanka LFL growth of 81% YoY in Q2

items.statement: Popeyes SSG growth double-digit in Q2
items.quote: Popeyes also grew double-digit SSG.

items.statement: Domino’s India delivery LFL growth of 16.5% YoY in Q2
items.quote: Delivery like-for-like growth was 16.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Domino’s India pre-IndAS EBITDA margin improvement YoY and QoQ
items.quote: The pre-IndAS EBITDA margin of our India business has seen an improvement year-on-year and on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Domino’s Turkey PAT margin of 10.4% in Q2

items.statement: Consolidated PAT from continued operations grew 53.7% YoY in Q2
items.quote: Consolidated PAT from continued operations grew 53.7% year-on-year.

items.quote: We have brought it down post-GST reduction to Rs. 799. So, on selective products, we have taken some deeper cuts.

items.statement: Domino’s India demand strong; sourdough pizza gaining traction in Tier-2/3 cities
items.quote: I am ac tually surprised by the uptake of sourdough pizza in Tier-2, Tier-3 cities. I would have never imagined that

items.quote: Our internal estimates suggest whatever between 65% to 70% market share, we continue to be there and growing.

items.statement: Shift from value products (e.g., Big Big Pizza) to premium (e.g., sourdough pizza) improving margins
items.quote: We believe now we are shifting mix, which was driving volumetric growth towards mix that is driving more ticket size.

items.quote: There is some inflation that we have been hit on the cheese prices, because milk prices post the Maharashtra election have really shot up.

items.statement: Lightweighting vertical revenue contribution to total revenue is ~10% currently, expected to grow significantly with new orders
items.quote: the lightweighting part of it is roughly 10% of revenues. items.statement: New lightweighting orders worth US$14M annual, US$70M lifetime value, SOP in Q1 FY28
items.quote: We are happy to announce 2 new orders in lightweighting vertical for control arms and links having combined annual value of US$14 million and lifetime value of US$70 million with SOP expected in Q1FY28.

items.statement: New global business order worth US$4.8M annual, US$24M lifetime value, SOP in Q4 FY27
items.quote: Our global business vertical established last year also continues to gain traction with another order with annual value of US$4.8 million and lifetime value of US$24 million from a customer added in quarter 1. SOP expected in Q4 FY27 with gradual ramp-up over 2 years post SOP.

items.statement: Export order delayed by 2 quarters due to customer inventory prebuying
items.quote: we expect that order to start 2 quarters after previously announced. So there should be around a 2-quarter delay, and that is not much to do with tariffs. The end product SOP is going to start 2 quarters later than planned by the end customer.

items.statement: EBITDA margin impacted by product mix, higher brick prices, and increased employee costs
items.quote: EBITDA margins, these are broadly in the range of 13% to 14%. In Q2, these were at 12.8%. And in first half, if you look at, these were 12.9%. items.statement: Input costs increased due to higher prices of noble metals in catalysts
items.quote: input cost has gone up. So if you see, the top line is made up of catalyst which also reflects in the RMC and the prices of catalyst have gone up due to the increase in prices of the underlying metals, which is the primary reason for increase in input cost.

items.statement: Strong demand momentum in passenger vehicles (PV) and light commercial vehicles (LCV) post GST cuts and festive season

items.statement: Positive demand outlook for PV and LCV segments

items.statement: Shift towards lightweighting and powertrain-agnostic components in PV segment

items.statement: TREM5 notification delay likely, but no formal communication on changes

items.statement: M&A conversations ongoing, focused on lightweighting vertical and powertrain-agnostic components

items.statement: Kit value per vehicle for suspension products ranges from INR 6,000 to INR 18,000

items.statement: Strong export traction in U.S., Europe, and Middle East markets
items.quote: It is surprisingly good. And that is indicative that we just got another big order, which we announced as part of this call. And even we have gotten confirmation for the previous order that the customer is going ahead and a lot of good traction as well in terms of RFQs and so on.

items.statement: Export order book includes CV emission components, temperature-controlled tubes, heat shields, and genset emission components
items.quote: Within exports, we have a focus on CV emissi on components, temperature- controlled tubes, heat shields, tractor and genset emission components

items.quote: there are for Para-IV filings for generic drugs and we are doing some clinical trials for first-time generics in India.

items.statement: Risdiplam (neurology) launch doing reasonably well; niche market
items.quote: Risdiplam , which is also doing reasonably well. It is not a large product, but nevertheless, it will strengthen the base business

items.quote: So that forecast remains intact combined with some growth from our existing lines of businesses that we have, we still expect FY '27 sales to be approximately between INR725 crores to INR750 crores.

items.statement: Industrial segment demand growing due to tire industry's carbon neutrality push

items.statement: Infrastructure segment demand expected to bounce back in Q3-Q4 FY26
items.quote: Yes, we are witnessing. I mean, Q3 should del iver good on the infrastructure. There is a bounce back. And we feel that Q3, Q4, there is bit a good amount of -- on the infrastructure side, this business will further bounce

items.quote: We believe in FY '27, the rCB Pyro business to contribute about INR100 crores, INR125 crores to our top line.

items.quote: So yes, there is -- we are probably 2 quarters behind in terms of starting the work in Saudi Arabia. But I don't see that to bring about any major challenge.

items.quote: We expect the rCB and the pyrolysis plant to be approximately 4 to 5 year kind of payback at this point of time.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton expected to reach INR 1,000+ at 70% utilization in FY27 (including solar)
